title: sigma_org_audit: QUERY_HISTORY/ACCESS_HISTORY proc to trace Sigma workbook access to writeback tables via embedded query comments
description:
Sigma appends a rich JSON comment (prefixed '-- Sigma Σ ') to the end of generated SELECT/INSERT queries, containing kind, email, sourceUrl (workbook URL), and request-id. Add a Snowflake proc that scans SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY joined to ACCESS_HISTORY (via LATERAL FLATTEN on OBJECTS_MODIFIED for inserts and BASE_OBJECTS_ACCESSED for reads), parses that trailing comment out of QUERY_TEXT with TRY_PARSE_JSON, and surfaces which workbooks/users actually read or wrote each writeback table. This gives ground-truth lineage (query-history-backed) to complement/validate the WAL-watermark-based orphan/stale heuristic in V_WRITEBACK_GOVERNANCE (see sigma_sandpit-su8) — i.e. a table with no WAL rows but real recent SELECT/INSERT traffic tied to a live workbook is NOT orphaned.

Mark has already drafted the working query format (see design field) scoped to a --DATABASE--.--WRITEBACK_SCHEMA--.% object filter and a rolling 7-day window; needs generalizing into a parameterized proc (schema/date-range args) and landing as raw/marts-layer SQL alongside the existing writeback scan (sigma_writeback_scan.sql) and marts procs (jww).

Land as a new proc file in sql/ (or wherever sigma_org_audit SQL procs live), wired into the existing extract/marts flow, and referenced in audit_queries.sql for the writeback governance section.
design:
SCORING-MATRIX INTEGRATION (enhancement, not replacement; agreed with Mark 2026-07-17):

Principle: query-history attribution is a HIGH-WEIGHT positive marker when PRESENT, and strictly NEUTRAL when ABSENT (no access data must never increase an orphaned/archival score -- absence = inconclusive, fall back to existing WAL logic). Every access-derived value is provenance-tagged so it's visible the signal came from ACCESS_HISTORY vs WAL.

Additive attributes on V_WRITEBACK_GOVERNANCE (new columns, nothing removed): ACCESS_WORKBOOK_ID / ACCESS_WORKBOOK_COUNT, LAST_READ_AT, LAST_WRITE_AT, READ_COUNT, WRITE_COUNT, DISTINCT_USERS, HAS_RECENT_ACCESS, ATTRIBUTION_SOURCE ('wal' | 'access_history' | 'both' | 'none').

Matrix changes:
1. ATTRIBUTION: add a high-priority branch BEFORE the ORPHANED fallthrough -- if a query-history workbook mapping exists, classify OWNED (this is the high-scored marker that rescues WAL-absent tables, the su8 fix), tagged ATTRIBUTION_SOURCE='access_history'/'both'.
2. IS_STALE: NOT stale if recent workbook-attributed access within the window, regardless of WAL edit timestamp.
3. ARCHIVAL_SCORE: recent access applies a strong NEGATIVE weight (drives score toward 0). Absence of access = no change to score.
4. Provenance: keep WAL-derived and access-derived attribution distinguishable in the output so a reviewer can see WHY a table is OWNED.

Net: WAL heuristic stays as-is and remains the fallback; access-history overlays a dominant OWNED/active signal where available, and can only ever make a table look MORE owned / less archivable, never more orphaned.

title: sigma_org_audit: deletion/tombstone detection (objects removed in Sigma must stop showing as live)
description: Foundational correctness, affects every object. Append-only plus latest-snapshot-wins means a deleted object keeps showing its last-seen state forever, and SCD2 never closes a vanished key. Add presence-diffing per snapshot so objects absent from the newest snapshot are tombstoned (IS_DELETED plus DELETED_AT) in stage/marts and closed in SCD2. Without this the inventory overcounts and drift misses deletions.

V_INVENTORY now carries IS_CURRENT/IS_DELETED/LAST_SEEN so deleted objects are flagged not shown-as-live; V_OWNERSHIP_CLEANUP filters to IS_CURRENT. title: writeback_info_dbx: enrich workbook/data-model → input-table lineage using system.access.table_lineage + query.history
description:
Improve the relationship tracking between Sigma workbooks/data models and their backing input tables by mining Databricks system tables instead of (or alongside) static WAL/API extraction.

Approach: join system.access.table_lineage to system.query.history on statement_id, scoped to the target schema, to get a history of SELECTs against each input table:

SELECT
  tl.event_time,
  tl.created_by,
  tl.source_table_full_name,
  tl.entity_type,
  tl.entity_metadata,
  tl.direct_access,
  qh.statement_text,
  qh.statement_type,
  qh.executed_by,
  qh.execution_status
FROM system.access.table_lineage tl
LEFT JOIN system.query.history qh
  ON tl.statement_id = qh.statement_id
WHERE tl.event_date >= CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL 90 DAYS  -- partition prune
  AND tl.event_time >= NOW() - INTERVAL 90 DAYS           -- precise boundary
  AND tl.source_table_schema = "marko_wb"
  AND tl.source_type = 'TABLE'
  AND qh.statement_type = 'SELECT'
ORDER BY tl.event_time DESC

Sigma tags every query it issues with a trailing SQL comment identifying the origin workbook/data model, e.g.:

-- Sigma Σ {"sourceUrl":"https://app.sigmacomputing.com/marko-eutest/data-model/model-dbx-test-viQz50PbiSg7zYkxBgo4P?:displayNodeId=NRYAsMEvRF","kind":"adhoc","request-id":"g019f7ffd18cb7663be0482ea7e3b8205","user-id":"8UomPZMREmTZLfEXBtb0WC0na36f0","email":"mark.oldfield@sigmacomputing.com"}

-- Sigma Σ {"sourceUrl":"https://app.sigmacomputing.com/marko-eutest/workbook/My-Workbook-DBX-Test-527Ldxl0hT3JKHuLw1USp4?:displayNodeId=fk0QY3zA9x","kind":"adhoc","request-id":"g019f7ffffca17d48bb72fa941d39d5ac","user-id":"8UomPZMREmTZLfEXBtb0WC0na36f0","email":"mark.oldfield@sigmacomputing.com"}

Parse this comment out of qh.statement_text to extract sourceUrl (distinguishing /workbook/ vs /data-model/ paths + slug/ID), kind, request-id, user-id, email. Use sourceUrl to positively attribute each SELECT back to the specific workbook or data model driving it, and cross-check against source_table_schema/entity_metadata to validate lineage is against the expected schema.

This is the Databricks-side analog of the query-history enrichment already shipped for sigma_org_audit writeback governance (SF, commit 93ac3bb / bd hvj) — same idea, different system tables (SF ACCOUNT_USAGE/QUERY_HISTORY vs DBX system.access.table_lineage + system.query.history) and a different tag-parsing regex (Sigma comment JSON differs from SF's).

Design questions to resolve during implementation:
- Where does the parsed history live — new mart table, or enrichment columns on existing SIGDS_WORKBOOK_MAP-equivalent?
- Cadence: on-demand query vs scheduled ingestion job (job.yml under resources/)?
- How to handle kind != 'adhoc' (e.g. scheduled/materialization queries) if they use a different tag shape.
close_reason: Delivered v1: writeback_info_dbx/sql/query_history_lineage.sql -- joins system.access.table_lineage x system.query.history on statement_id, parses the trailing '-- Sigma Σ {...}' comment (get_json_object) to recover sourceUrl/kind/request-id/user-id/email, and distinguishes /workbook/ vs /data-model/ source URLs (SF's stage_views.sql STG_WRITEBACK_ACCESS only handled /workbook/). Creates V_SIGMA_QUERY_LINEAGE (raw, one row per statement x table), V_SIGMA_QUERY_LINEAGE_SUMMARY (rolled up to SIGDS_TABLE + SCAN_SCHEMA grain, joinable onto SIGDS_WORKBOOK_MAP), and a cross-check query flagging tables the WAL heuristic marked for cleanup that were nonetheless actively SELECTed in the last 90 days. Design decisions resolved: (1) delivered as ad-hoc SQL views following the existing archival_scoring.sql/geninfo_queries.sql pattern, not wired into the scheduled job -- no landing/ingestion step needed since Unity Catalog system tables persist their own retention (unlike Snowflake ACCOUNT_USAGE which sigma_query_history_scan.sql has to land into raw first); (2) kind!='adhoc' rows are surfaced via LINEAGE_ATTRIBUTION_SOURCE rather than silently dropped. README updated (Files table + new 'Query-History Lineage' section with prereqs/caveats). Not yet validated against a live Databricks workspace -- SQL is written to spec but system.access.table_lineage / system.query.history schemas weren't available to test against in this session.

title: sigma_org_audit: add SCD2_DATAMODELS history table + V_DATAMODEL_DRIFT view (data models missing from SCD2 pipeline)
description:

title: sigma_org_audit: writeback scan misses OAuth multi-writeback schemas not enumerated for the audit credential — add warehouse-metadata schema discovery
description:
OAuth data connections support MULTI-writeback: multiple writeback schemas per connection, and the schema list an end user receives is scoped to the schemas they have access to. sigma_writeback_scan discovers scan targets purely from connection_detail (GET /v2/connections/{id}) writebackSchemas/writebacks (+ inputTableAuditLogSchema). Two gaps for OAuth:

1. DISCOVERY (API): if writebackSchemas is returned scoped to the calling credential's access, the audit client only sees the schemas IT can access — other users' writeback schemas on the same connection are never added to the scan target list. (Verify: does GET /v2/connections/{id} return all writeback schemas to an admin client, or only the caller's? Check docs + the extracted connection_detail payload.)
2. REACHABILITY (warehouse): even discovered schemas need USAGE+SELECT for the audit role to deep-scan; per-user OAuth schemas often aren't granted → SCAN_REACHABLE=FALSE (API-inventoried only).

Proposed fix: add warehouse-metadata-driven discovery as a supplement to the API list — for each connection's writeback database(s), query INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA / TABLES for any schema containing SIGDS_WAL_* (and SIGDS_*) tables, union with the API-reported locations, dedup, then scan. Makes coverage robust to per-user API scoping as long as the role can see the DB. Also: document granting the audit role on all writeback schemas (setup_prerequisites), and consider reporting discovered-but-not-in-API schemas as a signal. Relates to sigma_sandpit-qna (cross-account/non-Snowflake unreachable scans). Can't be tested locally — branch -> PR -> run.
close_reason: Premise invalidated by domain owner: OAuth multi-writeback schemas are defined at the CONNECTION level (not per-user-scoped away from an admin caller), so GET /v2/connections/{id} returns the full set to the audit credential. The scan already handles multiple entries — writebackSchemas/writebacks arrays are unioned + deduped and each (db,schema) is scanned (sigma_writeback_scan.sql L134-145, L254). Residual point (audit Snowflake role needs USAGE+SELECT per schema, else SCAN_REACHABLE=FALSE) is existing, documented behaviour and the cross-account variant is tracked by sigma_sandpit-qna. Metadata-discovery fallback idea preserved here if ever needed for defense-in-depth.

Validated live against the real Databricks workspace (customer_success.marko, schemas marko_wb/mo_dev/mo_prod). Confirmed: system.access.table_lineage does have source_table_name; the system schemas were already enabled/granted; ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMNS works cleanly against the existing SIGDS_WORKBOOK_MAP; watermark/incremental scan resumes correctly on repeat runs (no re-scan, no duplicate landing, confirmed by rerunning twice with stable row counts); full pipeline now runs clean across all 3 real schemas with real LINEAGE_* enrichment landing (WORKBOOK_ and DATA_MODEL-kind URLs both correctly distinguished).

Found + fixed 4 real bugs the design/code review missed, none of which were about the things originally flagged as risks:
1. Phase 8's broad except Exception silently swallowed a crash and misreported it as 'likely missing grant' -- job showed SUCCESS while doing nothing.
2. regexp_extract returns '' not NULL on no match -- broke IS_TAGGED and, combined with array indexing, threw INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX under this workspace's ANSI SQL mode for any /workbook/ URL (the common case, not just untagged rows). UPDATE SET */INSERT * broke on every run once Phase 8 widened SIGDS_WORKBOOK_MAP's schema (Delta star-merge requires source to supply every target column) -- fixed with explicit column lists generated from MERGE_SCHEMA/field_names, same single-source-of-truth pattern as the C1 fix.
